Neat idea but with all the claims about low cost to run and what not it comes out the product is 0.625 cents per gram compared to 0.32 for the traditional farm. I know they said fresher but they would still need to work on taller and efficiency (cost) to truly compete.

I think of it more as convenient farming for areas that aren't ideal for traditional farming. Some countries import most of their produce because they lack the space for farm land. Then there issues of low water climates, low fertile soil, or simply harsh weather climates for certain produce.

This isn't about replacing existing farms but a pretty sweet step towards creating farms in areas we couldn't before.

They is why I mention the height needing to be improved, you need to make the most of the small footprint by going up and in very high density 3 stories is not that much. In general would it be worth it to put the farm there or to put a business use the profit from that to import the goods, it is not a self sustaining system but most of the time places do not need to be self sustaining anymore. if you want something to last long term you can't run at ~2x the cost of your competition without offering something that that bulk of people will care about, and there is little that make people as a whole pay double for similar products. If they couldn't get the greens in while they were still good it would be different but that is not the case here.
Consider also that this is significantly cheaper to ship (if you need to ship at all) in the city.

I think of it this way: We have spent centuries, even millennia perfecting and making more efficient the growing of plants outdoors. This whole indoor vertical stuff is a relatively recent advancement, and a major change to the 'normal' way of doing things. The fact that the cost is already only twice that of the tried and true, perfected-over-millennia method is pretty astounding. Much like renewables vs non for energy, it won't take that long in the scheme of things for this to reach parity and eventually surpass older methods.
